post.description:
Validates the payload against the template's schema and queues a render.

By default this is asynchronous: it returns 202 with the document id and status; poll GET /v1/documents/:id until status is 'done', or receive a webhook.

Synchronous mode: send `Prefer: wait` (or `?wait=1`) to hold the response open until the render finishes, within a plan-bounded deadline. With `Accept: application/pdf` an unprotected document streams back as 200 application/pdf (the id is in the `X-Document-Id` header); otherwise you receive the 200 GET-shaped JSON (a `download` block for a finished document, or status + error for a failed one). If the deadline passes first, the response falls back to the async 202 and the render continues, so a later poll resolves the same id. Download-protected documents never stream inline: sync returns the JSON envelope pointing at the content endpoint.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Set to `1` for synchronous mode (same as the `Prefer: wait` header).

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: Set to `wait` for synchronous mode: the response blocks until the render is done, within a plan-bounded deadline, then falls back to the async 202. Equivalent to `?wait=1`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A unique token you generate per document (for example a UUID) so a retried request returns the original document instead of creating a duplicate. This is not authentication. Reuse it only for byte-for-byte equivalent render inputs: reusing it with a changed request returns 409. Equivalent to the `idempotencyKey` body field; if both are sent, this header wins.

200.description: Synchronous only: the finished document as JSON, or the raw PDF bytes when `Accept: application/pdf` was sent for an unprotected document.

202.description: Queued: the async default, or the synchronous deadline/fallback response.

get.description: Cursor-paginated history of documents this account generated, newest first. Filters: status, templateId, createdAfter/createdBefore (ISO date-time, bounding creation time), and delivery (the webhook-delivery state of each document: 'undelivered' for documents that were subscribed to a webhook but never delivered successfully — the set to reconcile after an endpoint outage — plus 'failed', 'delivered', 'pending', 'skipped', or 'none' for documents with no webhook). Pass include=url to attach a short-lived signed download URL to each finished document so you can list and fetch a missed window in one pass. Use the returned nextCursor to page.

post.description: Dry-run a payload against a template's JSON Schema and get pass or fail with error detail, without generating anything. Nothing is queued, no page is counted, and no usage is recorded, so an integrator or an agent can pre-flight its data (and repair it) for free before spending a render. Returns 200 with `{ ok, errors, version, schemaId, schemaVersion }`: `ok` is true when the payload satisfies the schema, otherwise `errors` lists what to fix. The response also echoes the exact version the check ran against, so validating and then generating pin the same contract.

200.description: The validation result: `{ ok, errors, version, schemaId, schemaVersion }`.

get.description: Poll a document. When status is 'done' the response includes a `download` block (a short-lived URL, or the password-gated content endpoint if the document is download-protected) plus `appliedOptions` (the per-render options it was created with).

Return a document's integrity proof: the SHA-256 `contentHash` of the issued PDF, its position in your account's append-only hash chain, and `chainVerified` (whether the chain link recomputes correctly from its predecessor). To check a file you hold, re-hash its bytes with SHA-256 and compare to `contentHash`, no API call is required for that. When the document was digitally signed, `signature` reports the algorithm, signer fingerprint, cert source, and whether the signer certificate is trusted; it is null for unsigned documents.

Return a signed provenance receipt for a completed document: an HMAC-signed JSON bundle binding the file to the request that produced it (`requestHash`), the pinned template version it was rendered against (`artifactHash`), who triggered it (`identity`), when it was issued, and the content fingerprint plus hash-chain link. A downstream party verifies it offline against the published key, without an API call. Available on paid plans; a completed document only.

Download a self-contained ZIP that proves a completed document offline, with no account and no network. It bundles the exact PDF, a machine-readable `manifest.json` of its integrity fingerprints, the frozen template that produced it, the request that was sent, and a static `verify.html` that re-hashes everything in the recipient's browser and reports pass or fail. It proves the bytes are unaltered and the template is the pinned version; it does not claim two renders are identical. Available on paid plans; a completed, not-yet-purged document only.

402.description: Proof packs are not available on the account's plan.

409.description: The document is not completed, or its PDF was purged.

post.description: Faithfully replay a prior document: the SAME version (or inline source), payload, options, and download protection. Regenerate cannot overwrite anything — it takes no request body (a non-empty body is rejected with 400) and returns a new document id (202), counting as a new render.

get.description: Stream a download-protected document's PDF. Supply the download password via the `X-Document-Password` header or HTTP Basic auth (any username). No API key is used. Returns 401 if the password is missing/wrong, 404 if the document isn't protected or isn't ready, 429 if too many attempts. All responses are `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

Current calendar-month page usage against plan quotas (feeds metered billing): billable API document pages (`pages`/`limit`) and editor PDF-preview pages (`previewPages`/`previewLimit`). Metered by page — a 10-page PDF counts as 10; failed renders aren't counted. Also returns the calling key's capability `scopes`, so a client (e.g. the CLI `login` command) can confirm the key and show what it may do.

All templates owned by the key's account (id, name, description, current published version, updatedAt), newest-updated first. `currentVersion` is 0 for a template that has never been published and so cannot be rendered yet. Authoring happens in the portal, not via the API.
Published version history of a template (newest first). Pin any of these via the `version` field on POST /v1/documents so a future edit can never alter a live integration.

One published version's metadata. Pass `?include=source` to also return the frozen editor source (compiled HTML + CSS, render settings, test data, pinned schema) — what `pageweaver pull` exports to round-trip a deployment. `read` scope; unknown version returns 404.

Export a change-control attestation for a published version: its compiled-artifact fingerprint (`artifactHash`), its position in the template's append-only artifact chain (`chainVerified`), the publish time and publisher, and the pinned schema version. Attach it to an audit package as proof the document contract was under formal version control. Available on paid plans; it proves an internal control trail, not a trusted digital signature.

A template's metadata: name, description, current published version, the associated schema + pinned schema version, and authoring mode. The key's account must own it (else 403); unknown id returns 404.
All payload schemas owned by the key's account (id, name, description, updatedAt). A schema may be reused by many templates and have many test datasets.
Published version history of a schema (newest first). Pin any of these via the `schemaVersion` field on POST /v1/documents.

One published version's metadata. Pass `?include=nodes` to also return the frozen typed field tree (FieldNode[]) — what `pageweaver pull` exports so a re-deployed schema matches. `read` scope; unknown version returns 404.

Returns the schema's name, description, and its PUBLISHED JSON Schema + sample for the latest published version (or `?version=N`). 409 if the schema has no published version yet. The key's account must own it (else 403).

post.description: Open an anchored comment thread on a generated document. Supply the `documentId`, an `anchorType` (point / area / text / page) with normalized 0-1 coordinates, and the opening message `body`. Returns 201 with the thread (including its first message).

get.description: The thread with its anchor, lifecycle state, and full (non-deleted) message history.

patch.description: Change a thread's severity, assignee, due date, or anchor coordinates (manual relocation). Lifecycle changes use the resolve/reopen/close routes, not PATCH.

post.description: Append a message to an open or resolved thread.
Mark an open thread resolved. 409 if it is not open.
Reopen a resolved thread. 409 if it is not resolved.
Close a thread (final — it can no longer change state).

get.description: Cursor-paginated comment threads on a document, newest first. Filter by pageNumber, status (open / resolved / closed), and severity (info / suggestion / blocking). Soft-deleted threads are never returned.

Per-page geometry (widthPts / heightPts) plus whether extracted text and a thumbnail exist — the denominators for normalized comment anchoring, so an integration can place comments without the viewer. Empty until post-render text extraction has run for the document.

post.description: Migrate the open comment threads from another document of the SAME template onto this one, as new linked threads (the originals are never modified). Each thread is re-anchored by a text-first ladder and tagged with a migration status and confidence; unplaceable threads are flagged for relocation. A regenerated document migrates its predecessor's comments automatically. Returns 202 (the migration runs in the background); poll the migration summary or the document's comments for the result.
post.summary: Carry comments forward from a previous document

get.description: Counts of the comment threads carried onto this document from an earlier version, grouped by migration status (migrated / resolved_by_change / needs_relocation / failed). Computed on read.

post.description: Request a review of a generated document. Supply the `documentId`, an optional `policy` (completion knobs), and `participants` (members and/or external reviewers). Creating a review retains the document until the review closes. Returns 201 with the review + policy state.

get.description: Filter by ?status= and ?documentId=; cursor paginated.
The request with its participants, append-only approvals, and current policy state.

post.description: Add a member (userId) or external reviewer (externalEmail + name).

Append an approval decision (approved / rejected / approved_with_comments). Returns 409 when the review policy forbids it (e.g. open blocking comments). Reaching the required approvers auto-completes the review.
Manually mark an open review completed. 409 if not open.
Withdraw an open review. 409 if not open.

Mint a capability-scoped link to a document or review request for an accountless external reviewer. The raw token is returned once in `url` and never stored (only its hash). Set `permissions` (canView/canComment/canDownload/canApprove/requireEmail/allowedDomains), an optional `password`, and an optional `expiresAt`.

get.description: Filter by ?documentId= or ?reviewRequestId=; cursor paginated. Tokens are never returned.

post.description: Kill switch: every subsequent open is refused and audited.

Freeze a candidate template change (inline `html`/`css`/`payloadSchema`, or `fromDraft: true` to use the saved draft). No new version is created and the current version does not advance. Returns 202 with the proposal; render-diff checks run asynchronously.

get.description: Filter by ?status=; cursor paginated (newest first).
The proposal with its status, check status/summary, append-only approvals, and promote-gate state.

delete.description: Withdraw an open proposal (only while open). The live version is untouched.

post.description: Re-run the render-diff regression (candidate vs. the live version, per saved dataset) and overwrite the check summary. Optional policy fields are persisted in checkSummary.regression. Only while the proposal is open. Byte-identical output is reported when it occurs, but is never claimed as the test (rendered output is not byte-reproducible).
Append an approval decision. Attribute it to a named approver via `approverUserId`, or omit it for an integration approval. The proposal author can never approve their own proposal.
Append a rejection decision and move the proposal to the rejected terminal state.

Publish the candidate as the next version through the serialized, gate-checked publish. Returns 409 when the approval gate is unmet, blocking comments are open, or the base version moved (the proposal is then superseded). Idempotent for an already-promoted proposal.

get.description: Every environment for the account, with pin counts.

post.description: Create a named pointer set (e.g. staging / production). Slug is the render-time selector.

patch.description: Rename or change the production flag. The slug is immutable.

delete.description: Deletes the environment and its pins (audited).

get.description: The template → version pointers in this environment.

put.description: Point a template at one of its published versions in this environment (creates or moves the pin).

delete.description: Unpin a template from this environment.

post.description: Copy another environment's pin set onto this one (e.g. staging → production). Pass `templates` to partial-promote. Version history is never touched — only pointers move.

Restore a prior deployment's pin set as a NEW pin-only deployment (history is never mutated). Pass `toDeploymentId` to target a specific deployment, or omit it to roll back to the last successful deployment before the current head. Only pointers move; no version is rebuilt.

Re-validate a manifest and its named file contents server-side, diff it against the target environment's live state, and persist a reviewable `planned` deployment. Returns 202 with the plan (a Terraform-style change list with before/after hashes); an unchanged manifest plans all no-op. Re-planning the same manifest at the same commit (or Idempotency-Key) returns the existing plan. Nothing is applied until POST /v1/deployments/:id/apply.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. For an ad-hoc plan without a commitSha, a unique token so a retried request returns the original plan instead of creating a duplicate.

post.description: Apply a previously planned deployment: publish the changed schema/template versions, write the target environment's pins, and record per-resource outcomes. Returns 202 with the deployment in `applying` (poll GET /v1/deployments/:id for the terminal `succeeded`/`failed`). Re-applying an in-flight or completed deployment returns it unchanged. A production deployment publishing a gate-on template without an approved proposal returns 409 listing the blocking templates.

get.description: Recent deployments for the account, newest first. Filter by `environment` slug.
One deployment with its per-resource plan lines and their apply outcomes.

post.description: Create a stable document identity from a template and issue its first version. Freezes the pinned template version + schema; reissuing later changes the data, never the design. Optionally publishes a public /d/:alias link. Returns the living-document id and the first version's queued document id (poll GET /v1/documents/:id).

get.description: Cursor-paginated list of this account's living documents, newest first.

post.description: Issue a new version under the same identity: the new payload is validated against the pinned schema and rendered; it supersedes the prior head and fires document.superseded. An invalid payload is rejected (400) and creates no new version.

get.description: One pinned version's metadata + integrity (the underlying document id, content hash, chain position).
The identity, its current head version, and the full ordered version history with per-version integrity.

All published forms owned by the key's account (id, name, slug, current version, and the pinned template + schema versions), newest-updated first. Draft-only forms are omitted. Authoring happens in the portal, not via the API.
Published version history of a form (newest first): version, snapshotHash, pinned template + schema, publish time.

post.description: Run a form's rules against a candidate payload and report validity WITHOUT metering, persisting, or rendering. Returns whether the data is valid, the validation messages, and the evaluated rule state (visible/required/computed values, included pages) so an integration can wire up field logic before sending a real submission. Rate-limited; a great CI check.

Submit a form's field values headlessly. The server evaluates the rules authoritatively (hidden fields are discarded, spoofed `_form` is ignored), validates against the pinned contract, and — when valid — renders the bound template into a document. Returns 202 with the submission id + status (`submitted` once queued, or `validation_failed`). Poll GET /v1/submissions/:id for the linked document. Requires the `render` scope; counts against your monthly submission limit.

get.description: A published form's metadata plus its machine-readable field contract: the pinned schema's compiled JSON Schema (the payload shape a submission must satisfy) and the ordered field summary (labels, steps, widgets). Pass include=source to also return the current version's frozen deployable source (named schema + template refs, layout, rules, tests) for a manifest export. The account must own it; unknown/unpublished ids return 404.

A submission's status (`submitted` / `validation_failed` / `rendered` / `delivered` / …), its data fingerprint, the linked document id (`renderJobId`) once accepted for render, and the validation messages when it failed. The account must own it; unknown id returns 404.
Lists the active account's document initiatives. Send `X-PageWeaver-Project` with a project id or slug to select the request context; omitting it selects the account's `default` project.

parameters.name: X-PageWeaver-Project
parameters.description: Account-local project id or slug for the request context. Omit it to use the account's `default` project.

info.title: PageWeaver API
info.description:
Generate PDFs from versioned templates and typed JSON payloads.

### Authentication
Every request must include your secret API key in the `x-api-key` header (`pk_live_...` in production, `pk_test_...` in development). This is the only credential the API needs. Create and roll keys in the portal.

### Idempotency
`POST /v1/documents` optionally accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header (or an `idempotencyKey` body field): a unique token you generate per document so that a retried request after a network error returns the original document instead of creating a duplicate. It is optional, and it is not authentication. If you send both, the header takes precedence.

### How rendering works
Creating a document is asynchronous by default. You receive `202` with a document id, then either poll `GET /v1/documents/:id` until the status is `done` or receive a webhook. The finished PDF is served from a short-lived download URL.

### Synchronous mode (Prefer: wait)
For a low-volume, latency-sensitive call you can get the result in one request: send the `Prefer: wait` header (or `?wait=1`) and the response blocks until the render finishes, within a plan-bounded deadline. With `Accept: application/pdf` an unprotected document streams back as `200 application/pdf` (its id is in the `X-Document-Id` response header); otherwise you receive the same `200` JSON that `GET /v1/documents/:id` returns. If the render takes longer than the deadline, the response falls back to the async `202` and keeps running, so a later poll of the same id still resolves. Sync is single-document only and meters identically to the async path; use async for bulk or long renders.

### Templates or inline HTML
Send a `templateId` to render a published template, or send inline `html` (plus optional `css`) to convert raw HTML directly. No external images, stylesheets, or JavaScript are allowed in inline HTML. Every document property (page, metadata, header/footer, watermark, localization, security) is overridable per request under the single `options` key.

### Download protection
Set `options.security.download` to require a password to download a document, separate from the PDF's own open-password. Protected documents are fetched from `GET /v1/documents/:id/content` with the `X-Document-Password` header (not the API key).

### Regenerate
`POST /v1/documents/:id/regenerate` faithfully replays a document exactly as it was (same version/inline source, payload, options). It accepts no body and cannot change the output.

tags.name: documents
tags.description: Create PDF documents from a template and a typed payload, then poll or receive a webhook for the result. This is the core endpoint.

tags.name: templates
tags.description: Discover your published templates and their pinnable versions. Read only. Author templates in the portal.

tags.name: schemas
tags.description: Discover the JSON Schemas your payloads are validated against, and their published versions. Read only.

tags.name: usage
tags.description: Check page consumption against your plan quota for the current period.

tags.name: comments
tags.description: Review generated documents: anchored comment threads, replies, and lifecycle (resolve / reopen / close). Requires an API key with the review scope.

tags.name: reviews
tags.description: Request reviews on generated documents, add participants, and collect approvals against a completion policy. Requires an API key with the review scope.

tags.name: share-links
tags.description: Create capability-scoped links so people without an account can view, comment on, or approve a document. Requires an API key with the review scope.

format.description: Output format. Default 'pdf'. png/jpeg/webp render a single image of the document.

width.description: Image viewport width in px. With only width set, the height grows proportionally.

height.description: Image viewport height in px. Pair with `clip` for an exact crop.

clip.description: Clip the image to width×height (an exact crop) instead of capturing the full page.

quality.description: Compression quality 1-100 (jpeg/webp only). Higher is clearer and larger.

transparent.description: Transparent background (png/webp only). Ignored for jpeg and pdf.

optimizeForSpeed.description: Trade some image quality for a faster capture.

pdfa.description: Archival PDF/A conformance. '2b' or '3b' produce a validated PDF/A; 'none' opts out of a template that defaults to archival output. Only b-level conformance is offered. Two consequences to know about: link annotations do not survive the conversion, and text set with OpenType feature substitution (for example `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) stops being extractable, so a PDF/A document is not a searchability guarantee. The `Author` metadata field is dropped, because it cannot be written in a way the standard permits. Adds roughly 200ms plus 25ms per page. Cannot be combined with an image format, a PDF open-password, a digital signature, or a `url` render.

singlePage.description: Collapse the whole document onto one tall page.

preferCssPageSize.description: Honor the document's CSS @page size over API paper params.

title.description: PDF Title (also the header/footer {{title}}). Liquid tokens resolve.

enabled.description: Show the band. Omitted + any slot text present auto-enables it.

color.description: Band text color (hex or CSS name).

outline.description: Emit PDF bookmarks/outline from the document headings.

userPassword.description: Password required to open the PDF (PDF encryption).

enabled.description: Apply a PAdES digital signature to this document.

reason.description: Optional reason shown in the signature panel.

location.description: Optional location shown in the signature panel.

contactInfo.description: Optional contact info shown in the signature panel.

certSource.description: Which certificate signs. 'platform' uses PageWeaver's issuer (valid signature, untrusted issuer badge); 'byo' uses your uploaded certificate for a trusted badge (available on Enterprise).

timestamp.description: Add a trusted timestamp (RFC 3161) to the signature, proving when it was signed independent of our clock. Included with signing.

enabled.description: Enable a download password that gates streaming the PDF from our CDN.

password.description: The download password recipients must supply to fetch the PDF.

generate.description: Generate a strong random download password (returned in the response).

signature.description: Digital signature: sign this document so it opens with a signed-and-unmodified badge in a PDF reader.

download.description: Download protection: a separate password that gates streaming this document from our endpoint, distinct from the PDF's own open-password. Overrides the template default per request.

mode.description: Route this document's storage delivery. 'all' = every enabled destination; 'none' = don't deliver this document; 'selected' = only the destinations in `destinationIds`. Overrides the template's delivery setting for this render.

destinationIds.description: Destination ids to deliver to when `mode` is 'selected'. Ids your account does not own are ignored.

rendering.description: Media type, backgrounds, page ranges, single page.

delivery.description: Direct-to-storage delivery routing (BYOS): which of your configured buckets this document is copied to. Overrides the template's delivery setting for this render only.

templateId.description: Template id (or the built-in 'sample-invoice'). Provide EXACTLY ONE content source: `templateId`, inline `html`, or `url`.

url.description: url-to-pdf: an https URL of a live web page to snapshot into a PDF. Mutually exclusive with `templateId` and `html`; no payload/schema/version. Every fetch is SSRF-checked (private and reserved hosts are blocked). Available on paid plans.

output.description: What this call produces. Use `format` for a raster image (png/jpeg/webp) instead of a PDF, with optional sizing / transparency / quality, and `pdfa` for archival PDF/A conformance. Omit for the default PDF. An image is not compatible with a `url` render or with PDF-only options (digital signature, PDF open-password, tagged PDF).

html.description: Inline render: raw HTML to convert directly, with no template. Mutually exclusive with templateId. No external images, stylesheets, or JavaScript are allowed (rejected with a 400). May use Liquid tokens + `payload`; account image assets are referenced by name.

css.description: Inline render only: CSS applied to the inline `html` (injected as a <style>). Requires `html`.

payload.description: Data merged via Liquid. For a template render it is validated against the template's JSON Schema (required). For an inline render it is optional and merged as-is (no schema).

version.description: Pin a published TEMPLATE version; defaults to the template's latest.

environment.description: Render the version this template is pinned to in the named environment (e.g. 'production'), instead of a numeric `version`. Mutually exclusive with `version`. Fails with 409 if the template has no pin in that environment (no silent fallback). Requires a `templateId`.

schemaId.description: Validate the payload against THIS schema instead of the one the template pins. Omit to use the template's pinned schema. The key's account must own the schema.

schemaVersion.description: Pin a published SCHEMA version (requires schemaId); defaults to that schema's latest published version.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency token you generate per document, so repeating a request returns the same document instead of creating a duplicate. This is not authentication. Prefer the `Idempotency-Key` header; this body field is a fallback for clients that cannot set headers. Reusing a key with different render inputs returns 409. If both are sent, the header wins.

callbackUrl.description: HTTPS URL to receive a signed POST when this render reaches a terminal state (done/failed). Overrides the account-default webhook for this render only. Polling still works regardless.

options.description: Per-render document properties, layered on the version's frozen settings for this render only. Nest every override under this one key (page / rendering / metadata / header / footer / watermark / structure / localization / security). Unknown keys are rejected (400).

templateId.description: Template id (or the built-in 'sample-invoice') whose schema the payload is checked against.

payload.description: The data to validate against the template's JSON Schema.

version.description: Check against a published TEMPLATE version; defaults to the template's latest.

environment.description: Check against the version this template is pinned to in the named environment (e.g. 'production'), instead of a numeric `version`. Mutually exclusive with `version`.

schemaId.description: Validate against THIS schema instead of the one the template pins. Your account must own it.

schemaVersion.description: Pin a published SCHEMA version (requires schemaId); defaults to that schema's latest.

offset.description: Character offset of the mention token in the body.

documentId.description: The document id this comment anchors to (from POST /v1/documents).

anchorType.description: How the comment is anchored: 'point' (a pin), 'area' (a rectangle), 'text' (a quoted selection), or 'page' (whole-page feedback).

pageNumber.description: 1-based page number (required for every anchor except a pure page comment on page 1).

selectedText.description: The quoted text a 'text' anchor refers to.

textBefore.description: ~64 chars of text before the selection (migration context).

textAfter.description: ~64 chars of text after the selection (migration context).

textHash.description: Page-text hash at creation (migration similarity input).

body.description: The opening message of the thread.

severity.description: Thread severity. 'blocking' can gate approval when a review policy says so. Default 'info'.

visibility.description: Who sees the thread: 'internal' (members only, default) or 'external' (also share-link reviewers).

assignedToUserId.description: Assign the thread to a member (their user id).

dueAt.description: Optional due date (ISO 8601) for the assignee.

mentions.description: Members mentioned in the opening message.

assignedToUserId.description: Assign to a member (user id), or null to unassign.

dueAt.description: Due date (ISO 8601), or null to clear.

pageNumber.description: Relocated page number (with the coordinates below).

fromDocumentId.description: The id of a previously generated document, from the SAME template, whose open comment threads should be carried forward onto this document. Both must belong to your account.

requireAllCommentsResolved.description: Every thread must be resolved before the review can auto-complete.

blockerCommentsPreventApproval.description: An open blocking-severity comment prevents approval + completion (default true).

requiredApproverCount.description: Distinct approvers required to complete the review (default 1).

allowApprovalWithOpenComments.description: When false, an approval is refused while any comment is open (default true).

userId.description: A member's user id (mutually exclusive with externalEmail).

externalEmail.description: An accountless external reviewer's email (mutually exclusive with userId).

externalName.description: Display name for an external reviewer.

role.description: Participant role: reviewer (default), approver, or observer.

title.description: A short title for the review.

message.description: An opening message to the participants.

dueAt.description: Optional due date (ISO 8601). Past-due open reviews are nudged, then expire.

policy.description: Completion policy (omit for the platform defaults).

userId.description: A member's user id (mutually exclusive with externalEmail).

externalEmail.description: An external reviewer's email (mutually exclusive with userId).

externalName.description: Display name for an external reviewer.

role.description: Participant role: reviewer (default), approver, or observer.

decision.description: The decision: approved, rejected, or approved_with_comments.

note.description: An optional note recorded with the decision.

approverUserId.description: Optionally attribute the decision to a member who is a named approver on this review. When omitted, the decision is recorded as an integration approval authorized by the key's review scope.

canView.description: May view the document (always granted; a link that shows nothing is meaningless).

canComment.description: May create + reply to external comments (default false).

canDownload.description: May download the PDF; when false the bytes are view-only streamed (default false).

canApprove.description: May record an approval decision on a shared review request (default false).

requireEmail.description: Require an email (not just a name) before the external reviewer can interact (default false).

allowedDomains.description: Restrict the email gate to these domains (e.g. ["acme.com"]); empty ⇒ any domain.

targetType.description: What the link grants access to.

documentId.description: The document to share (required when targetType = render).

reviewRequestId.description: The review request to share (required when targetType = reviewRequest).

permissions.description: Capability grants for the external actor.

password.description: Optional password gate (6–128 chars); stored scrypt-hashed.

expiresAt.description: Optional expiry (ISO 8601). Refused at open time; the sweeper hard-disables past it.

fromDraft.description: Freeze the template's current saved draft as the candidate (ignores the inline html/css).

html.description: Candidate template HTML (compiled Liquid). Required unless fromDraft.

payload.description: Example payload; used to infer the JSON Schema when payloadSchema is omitted.

payloadSchema.description: The candidate payload JSON Schema (the API contract). Inferred from payload when omitted.

editorMode.description: Authoring mode of the candidate (default code).

editorSource.description: Lossless re-editable restore source (visual mode). Omit for code mode.

renderSettings.description: Frozen Gotenberg render settings for the candidate version.

note.description: A short 'what changed' note, shown in history at promote (max 200).

regressionMode.description: Advisory allows changed output after review; strict makes changed fixture output a publish-readiness blocker.

checks.description: Observable regression signals to evaluate. Hash equality is a strong pass signal; hash inequality remains informational.

minSuccessfulFixtures.description: Minimum number of fixtures that must render successfully before publish readiness passes.

failOnErrors.description: When false, fixture render/schema errors remain visible but do not block publish readiness.

note.description: An optional note recorded with the decision (max 1000).

approverUserId.description: Attribute the decision to a member who is a named approver on a review targeting this proposal. When omitted, the decision is an integration decision authorized by the key's deploy scope.

slug.description: Stable API handle used as the render-time `environment` selector. Unique per account.

isProduction.description: Mark this the production environment (pins here get the approval-gated deploy treatment).
Whether this is the production environment.

version.description: The published template version this environment points at.

from.description: Source environment slug to copy pins from.

templates.description: Only promote these template ids. Omit to promote every pin in the source environment.

toDeploymentId.description: The deployment id whose pin set to restore. Omit to roll back to the last successful deployment before the current head.

environment.description: Target environment slug the plan diffs against and apply will write pins into.

files.description: Manifest-relative path → UTF-8 file contents for every file the manifest names (templates, schemas, test data). The CLI uploads only the referenced files, not the repository. Per-file and total size caps apply (mirroring the inline-render limits).

commitSha.description: The commit the manifest was rendered at. With a commitSha, re-planning the same manifest at the same commit returns the existing Deployment (idempotent). Omit for an ad-hoc plan.

sourceRef.description: Branch/tag/workflow-run ref for provenance, e.g. 'refs/heads/main' or a PR number.

source.description: Where the plan originated (provenance only). Defaults to 'cli'.

env.description: Optional environment values for resolving `${NAME}` references in the manifest (e.g. a webhook URL secret). Secrets are used to compute config hashes and are never stored or echoed back.

templateId.description: The template to render this living document from. Must have a published version.

version.description: Pin a specific published template version to freeze for this identity's whole life. Defaults to the template's current published version. Reissuing changes the data, never the design.

payload.description: The payload for the first issued version, validated against the pinned schema.

name.description: A human label for the living document.

publicAlias.description: Publish a public /d/:alias link that always resolves to the latest version. Requires the publicAlias plan capability. The alias is an unguessable capability token.

payload.description: The new payload for this version, validated against the identity's pinned schema.

data.description: The form field values to dry-run (the same shape a filler submits). Reserved `_form` is ignored.
The submitted form field values. Reserved `_form` is ignored; rule-hidden fields are discarded server-side.
